cards.explanation: The answer is anyone with a skin disease. It's in the LORD's command to Moses (Numbers 5:2). A bodily discharge and being defiled by a dead body ride in the same verse, so that one verse holds three groups. Short verse, big list, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp…" (Numbers 5:3) So it isn't only the men. Women are included too, friends.

The reason is so they won't defile the camp where He lives. The LORD says to send them outside "…so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them." (Numbers 5:3) Look at where the weight falls, bakers. It's the camp, and it's the fact that He dwells right there among them. The whole command is built around that.

The answer is True. The text says, "So the Israelites did this, sending such people outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had instructed Moses." (Numbers 5:4) No arguing and no dragging their feet is recorded. Just the command, and then the doing. I wish my dough did that.

The answer is LORD. The LORD says that when someone commits a sin against another, that person "…acts unfaithfully against the LORD…" (Numbers 5:6) So the sin lands on a neighbor, and it's also against Him. That's a lot packed into one verse, friends.

The first thing the guilty person must do is confess the sin he committed. The guilty person "…must confess the sin he has committed." (Numbers 5:7) Confession comes first, and the making right follows in the same verse. Owning up is hard, friends. I've watched a whole batch of cookies vanish off a cooling rack while I stood there covered in crumbs, and my first instinct was still to say "Wasn't me!"

The answer is a fifth of its value. The verse says, "He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value, and give all this to the one he has wronged." (Numbers 5:7) So it's the full amount, plus a fifth. Count it carefully, bakers, because the math matters.

The answer is False. The verse says that if there's no relative, "…the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest…" (Numbers 5:8) The guilty person doesn't get to hold on to it, friends. It goes to the priest, and it's the LORD's.

The answer is the priest. The restitution "…belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest along with the ram of atonement…" (Numbers 5:8) The priest is the one who receives it. And the ram is how the atonement is made for the guilty person, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, "Each man’s sacred gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest will belong to the priest." (Numbers 5:10) So until he gives them, they're his. After he gives, they're the priest's. It works like my cookie box: mine until I hand it over.
